meta.description: UI map of the generated production-ranges report. One template renders every report; most of the page is built by its inline script at runtime, so anchors point at the code that draws an element, not at static markup.
meta.generated: Read from templates/report.html on 2026-09-20. Every element carries a data-inspect-id (static markup) or dataset.inspectId (runtime-built), which is both the map anchor and the hook the inspector overlay reads.
meta.howToUse: locate.grep is a ready-to-paste grep command; run it from the repo root. locate.path is a secondary file:line reference that drifts as the file changes - the grep command does not.
rules: An inspect id is unique across the whole app, not just within its own component or page. The overlay resolves the first element carrying an id and stops, so two elements sharing one id leaves the second unreachable. Worse, the inspector then reports an element the reader is not looking at, with a description that does not match what is on their screen. On 2026-09-20 in nfl-props the shortlist pill reused the card pill's id. A request to move one moved the other, and two rounds were spent describing different parts of the page to each other before the cause surfaced.

A function that emits an element and is called from more than one place must take its id as a parameter. Reusing markup is good; reusing the id that identifies it is not. This is the shape the 2026-09-20 duplicate took, and it is the one a uniqueness grep cannot catch, because the id appears exactly once in the source.
When one id is a prefix of others (prematch-rank-drum against prematch-rank-drum-up), anchor the grep on the full attribute so it cannot match a child.
Every entry here is added, renamed or removed in the same change as the element it describes. A map that lags the code is worse than no map: it answers confidently and wrongly.
meta.inspector: Attached to every report by scripts/serve_reports.py. Press the crosshair button, bottom right, to arm it. The button remembers its state across reloads. The overlay is injected per request and never written into the report files themselves. A theme switch (auto / light / dark) is injected the same way, bottom left; like the crosshair it is page chrome and carries no inspect id.

nodes.label: Production ranges report
nodes.description: The single report template. Placeholders (__DATA__, __META__, __TARGET__, __TITLE__, __EYEBROW__, __HEADLINE__, __TARGET_ABS__) are string-replaced at build time; everything else is drawn client-side from DATA. The likeliest touchdown scorer is not baked in: scripts/serve_reports.py injects window.__TD__ at serve time, and the script tints that player's cards. Results arrive the same way, as window.__ACTUALS__, and only once the game is final.

uiElements.label: Page container
uiElements.description: Outer 1120px column that everything on the report sits inside.

uiElements.label: Report header
uiElements.description: Top block holding the eyebrow line and the matchup headline.

uiElements.label: Kickoff eyebrow
uiElements.description: Kickoff time, week and season. Filled at build time from __EYEBROW__ in nflprops/report.py.

uiElements.label: Chart legend
uiElements.description: Explains the two team colours, the shaded middle-68% band, the dashed expected line, and the solid FanDuel line.

uiElements.label: Shortlist panel
uiElements.description: Black-bordered panel holding the ranked shortlist and its payout footer.

uiElements.label: Shortlist heading
uiElements.description: 'The shortlist' with the 'most confident first' unit label.

uiElements.label: Shortlist caveat
uiElements.description: States that confidence means likely, not mispriced. This is the disclaimer, not decoration.

uiElements.label: Shortlist list
uiElements.description: Empty <ol> in the template. Filled at runtime from every DATA row carrying a pick number.

uiElements.label: Shortlist row
uiElements.description: One leg: rank, player, bet and line, price, confidence percent.

uiElements.label: Payout footer
uiElements.description: Straight payout, naive joint chance, and the correlation note.

uiElements.label: Straight payout
uiElements.description: Product of every leg's decimal odds. Computed in the template's own script, not server-side.

uiElements.label: Naive joint chance
uiElements.description: Product of min(model, book) across legs. 'Naive' because it assumes independence.

uiElements.label: Correlation note
uiElements.description: Whether the legs share a game. Text chosen in nflprops/report.py and injected via META.corrnote.

uiElements.label: Stat sections container
uiElements.description: Empty div. Runtime appends one heading plus one card grid per stat in STATS.

uiElements.label: Stat section heading
uiElements.description: Stat name plus its unit, e.g. 'Rushing yards / yards'.

uiElements.label: Player card grid
uiElements.description: Responsive grid of player cards for one stat, ordered by how close the book's number sits to the curve's peak.

uiElements.label: Player card
uiElements.description: One player-stat projection. Gets a heavier border when it is a shortlist pick.

uiElements.label: Card player name
uiElements.description: Player name in the card's top row. Wraps onto a second line rather than truncating, so a long name is always shown in full.

uiElements.label: Card role badge
uiElements.description: Team-coloured position badge, e.g. QB1 or WR2.

uiElements.label: Card main column
uiElements.description: Left column of the card head: name and position, the expected number, and the range under it. Sits beside the flag stack so the two share the head's height.

uiElements.label: Card identity column
uiElements.description: Left half of the card head: the player's name and his position badge.

uiElements.label: Card flag stack
uiElements.description: Top-right column of the card. Holds the five-dot record, then the pick and td badges stacked below it. The old-vs-new engine line no longer lives here; it sat here until 2026-09-24 and its width squeezed the player name.

uiElements.label: Card record dots
uiElements.description: Last five calls we published on this player and stat, most recent on the left. Green cleared the line, red did not, grey means no number was offered. A hollow dot is a week we never made the call.

uiElements.label: Card record dot
uiElements.description: One week of that record. Hover gives the week, the real number, and how it went.

uiElements.label: Card pick badge
uiElements.description: Only present when the player is on the shortlist. Shows the pick's rank.

uiElements.label: Card expected value
uiElements.description: The projection's mu, after calibration.

uiElements.label: Card range
uiElements.description: The middle-68% band, mu plus or minus one sd, with sd already widened 10%.

uiElements.label: Card curve chart
uiElements.description: Inline SVG Gaussian. Built by curve() from mu and sd alone.

uiElements.label: Curve hover target
uiElements.description: Transparent rect that catches mousemove and drives the tooltip. The chart has no other pointer handling.

uiElements.label: Model vs book row
uiElements.description: FanDuel's line and price against the model's and book's implied probabilities.

uiElements.label: Model vs book, no line
uiElements.description: Shown instead of the comparison when no price near the target was offered for this player-stat.

uiElements.label: Peak offset note
uiElements.description: How many standard deviations separate the book's number from the curve's peak.

uiElements.label: Matchup note
uiElements.description: Defensive multiplier versus this position. Marked 'context only' for receiving stats, where applying it made projections worse.

uiElements.label: Curve tooltip
uiElements.description: Fixed-position readout that follows the cursor across a curve, showing a value and the chance of more.

uiElements.label: Full table disclosure
uiElements.description: Collapsed section holding every projected figure, not just the featured cards.

uiElements.label: Full table toggle
uiElements.description: Click target that expands the full figures table.

uiElements.label: Full figures table
uiElements.description: Every DATA row: player, role, stat, expected, minus and plus one sd, spread, matchup.

uiElements.label: Table row
uiElements.description: One player-stat row in the full table.

uiElements.label: Footer notes
uiElements.description: Four explanatory blocks: reading the matchup figure, curve width, model versus book, and the 'these are not edges' disclaimer.

uiElements.label: Touchdown scorer card
uiElements.description: The likeliest touchdown scorer's player card, washed in that player's team colour so the eye finds them before reading a name. Every card for that player is tinted, one per stat.

uiElements.label: Card touchdown badge
uiElements.description: Confidence chip on a tinted card, e.g. 'td 55%'. The lower of the model's number and the book's, the same rule every leg follows.

uiElements.label: Card Phase 3 combined-TD number
uiElements.description: 'new td X%': the new (Phase 3, decision #30) touchdown model's number, under the old engine's td badge. The old number stays primary: each game's top-ranked scorer hit 45% (old) vs 41% (new) over 2021-2025.

uiElements.label: Card Phase 3 volume/yardage number
uiElements.description: The old-vs-new engine line, under the card's range: 'old engine X · new model Y (+/-gap)'. Old engine = nflprops/project.py (first model, 2026-09-13), which also makes the card's big number. New model = the Phase 3 ridge model (decision #31, added 2026-09-24; extended to receptions decision #38, and to passing_yards decision #39, both 2026-09-24). Covers receiving_yards, rushing_yards, receptions, and passing_yards. Gap is new minus old. Shaded (.big) when |gap| >= half the card's spread (decision #37). Never merged into one figure. Head-to-head 2021-2025 is a near-tie on three of the four: receiving MAE 22.82 vs 22.84, rushing 21.30 vs 21.44, receptions 1.65 vs 1.65. Passing yards is not a tie -- old 67.09 vs new 62.56 MAE (n=3,107), new model won all 5 seasons tested. Absent if data/shipping/{targets,carries,receiving_yards,rushing_yards,passing_yards}.pkl are missing.

uiElements.label: New model's expected, on the curve
uiElements.description: Purple (--p3) dashed rule at the Phase 3 new model's number (d.p3), same height as the old engine's team-coloured dashed mean line. Pinned to the edge, finer dash, when outside the drawn range. Absent when d.p3 is null (no shipping pickles for that stat). The curve itself is still the old engine's.

uiElements.label: Back to all reports
uiElements.description: Link at the very top of the report, above the header, back to the listing at /. A report is often opened cold from a Slack link, where the browser's own back button leads nowhere.

uiElements.label: Actual pill
uiElements.description: Filled pill on a player card's headline row, beside the number the model expected. Carries the number the player actually put up; green means it beat the line, red means it did not. Fixed width so a one-digit and a three-digit actual make the same block. Drawn for every projected player with a line, not only the shortlisted ones. The values arrive as window.__ACTUALS__, spliced in by scripts/serve_reports.py at serve time -- a report is written before kickoff and never rewritten, so the outcome cannot be baked in. Hover text and aria-label say hit or miss in words, since colour alone is not readable to everyone.

uiElements.label: Actual on the curve
uiElements.description: Vertical rule drawn on a player's curve at the number he actually put up, with a dot at its foot. Green cleared the betting line, red did not, grey means no number was offered on that stat. The pill says whether the leg won; this says whether the projection was any good -- a leg can win with the real figure way out in the tail. A figure past the drawn range is pinned to the edge and dashed.

uiElements.label: Actual key
uiElements.description: The curve legend's entry for the actual-result rule, saying what green, red and grey mean.

uiElements.label: Legend: new model's expected
uiElements.description: Purple dashed swatch keying the new model's rule on the curves. The 'expected' key beside it now reads 'old engine's expected (team colour)'.

uiElements.label: Shortlist actual pill
uiElements.description: The pill itself on a shortlist row. Same markup as the card pill, under its own id so the inspector can tell the two apart.

uiElements.label: Shortlist actual
uiElements.description: The same pill on a shortlist row, sitting directly after the leg it grades rather than at the far end of the row. The slot keeps its width when a game has not finished, so the rows stay a column while results land one game at a time.

uiElements.label: Shortlist old vs new numbers
uiElements.description: 'old X · new Y' on each shortlist row: old engine (d.mu, team colour) and new model (d.p3, purple, '—' when none, e.g. receptions). Same colours as the curve lines. Hidden under 560px width.

nodes.label: Report listing
nodes.description: The listing at /. Built by index_html() from the PAGE constant in this file -- there is no template. Weeks are tabs, left to right as played, newest selected. Cards are split into one block per kickoff time inside a week. Game cards deliberately mirror the player card in templates/report.html; if that card's anatomy moves, move this with it. The tab script is the separate TABS_JS constant, kept out of PAGE so its braces need no escaping.

uiElements.label: Listing container
uiElements.description: Outer 720px column holding the whole listing.

uiElements.label: Listing eyebrow
uiElements.description: Small monospace line above the title, matching the eyebrow on a report.

uiElements.label: Listing title
uiElements.description: The 'NFL Props' headline, in the same condensed face as a report's matchup headline.

uiElements.label: Listing subtitle
uiElements.description: Explains the tabs, the ordering, the TD marker, and that no edge is being claimed.

uiElements.label: Week tab strip
uiElements.description: Row of week tabs, reading left to right in the order the weeks were played. Arrow keys move between them, Home and End jump to the first and last.

uiElements.label: Week tab
uiElements.description: One week's tab, with that week's game count beside the label. The newest week sits on the right and is the one selected on load.

uiElements.label: Week panel
uiElements.description: The card grid for one week. Every panel but the selected one carries the hidden attribute.

uiElements.label: Game card
uiElements.description: One game's card, linking through to its report. Built on the same anatomy as a report's player card: label and badge on top, an oversized figure, a range line, then a dotted comparison row.

uiElements.label: Card game label
uiElements.description: The away-at-home pairing in the card's top row, where a player card puts the player's name.

uiElements.label: Card day badge
uiElements.description: Accent-coloured weekday, e.g. SUN. Sits where a player card puts the position badge. Absent when no schedule row exists.

uiElements.label: Card kickoff time
uiElements.description: Kickoff time as the card's headline figure, where a player card puts its projection. Falls back to 'kickoff unknown' rather than the file's timestamp.

uiElements.label: Card date line
uiElements.description: Timezone and date under the figure, where a player card puts its range.

uiElements.label: Empty listing message
uiElements.description: Replaces the tabs and panels entirely when no reports have been generated yet.

uiElements.label: Listing footer
uiElements.description: The standing disclaimer: projections, not edges, and less accurate than the market in testing.

uiElements.label: Kickoff block
uiElements.description: All the games that kick off at one time, e.g. every Sunday 1:00 PM game. A Sunday is four separate sittings, and one undivided grid hid that.

uiElements.label: Kickoff block label
uiElements.description: Day and time for one block, with its game count. Quieter than a week tab, louder than a card.

uiElements.label: Slate link
uiElements.description: Takes the reader from the listing to the consolidated slate at /slate.

uiElements.label: Explore link
uiElements.description: Takes the reader from the listing to /explore, the grouped results page.

uiElements.label: Game card, no report
uiElements.description: Dashed, dimmed, non-clickable card for a scheduled game that has no report yet.

uiElements.label: Game label, no report
uiElements.description: The matchup on a pending card, in the dimmed weight.

uiElements.label: No-report marker
uiElements.description: Hollow dashed "N/A" pill on a pending card, in the same slot and the same 18px box the hit tally uses once the game is reported and played. Full wording is in its title attribute.

uiElements.label: Hit tally badge
uiElements.description: How the game's shortlisted picks did once it finished, as a bare fraction like "5/6". Sits on the same line as the matchup, pinned to the card's right edge. Green when at least half landed, red when fewer did. The full wording is in its title attribute. Absent while a game is still being played.

nodes.label: Consolidated slate
nodes.description: Served at /slate. Pools every shortlisted leg in the newest week by sitting (Early / Afternoon / Night on each day) and ranks each sitting three ways: most likely, shortest odds, longest odds. Reads the picks back out of the report files on disk - no Odds API call, and no second copy of the picks that could drift from the report it came from.

uiElements.label: Slate container
uiElements.description: Outer 720px column holding the whole slate page.

uiElements.label: Slate eyebrow
uiElements.description: Season and week above the title.

uiElements.label: Slate title
uiElements.description: The page's H1: "The Slate".

uiElements.label: Slate subtitle
uiElements.description: Explains what Model, Book and the gap figure mean.

uiElements.label: Back to listing
uiElements.description: Returns to the report listing at /.

uiElements.label: Sitting section
uiElements.description: One section per day-part: every leg from the games kicking off in that sitting.

uiElements.label: Sitting heading
uiElements.description: Day chip, part of day, kickoff times, and the game/leg counts.

uiElements.label: Sitting day chip
uiElements.description: Accent-filled weekday chip on a sitting heading.

uiElements.label: Sitting kickoff times
uiElements.description: The kickoff times pooled into this sitting, e.g. "4:05, 4:25 PM ET".

uiElements.label: Ranking table block
uiElements.description: One of the three rankings inside a sitting: heading, note, table.

uiElements.label: Ranking title
uiElements.description: "Most likely to happen", "Shortest odds", or "Longest odds".

uiElements.label: Ranking note
uiElements.description: One line saying what the ranking is sorted by.

uiElements.label: Leg row
uiElements.description: One shortlisted leg: player, team/role, game, line, price, payout, model and book probability, and the gap between them.

uiElements.label: Slate empty state
uiElements.description: Shown when no reports have been generated at all.

uiElements.label: Slate no-kickoff state
uiElements.description: Shown when reports exist but none of their games has a schedule row to pool by.

uiElements.label: Slate footer
uiElements.description: Standing disclaimer: projections not edges, prices move.

uiElements.label: Slate week strip
uiElements.description: Tab strip, one week per tab, newest selected on load.

uiElements.label: Slate week tab
uiElements.description: Opens one week's sittings. The count is that week's shortlisted legs.

uiElements.label: Slate week panel
uiElements.description: All sittings for one week. Every week but the newest ships hidden.

uiElements.label: Sitting hit tally
uiElements.description: How the whole sitting's picks did, e.g. "5/6 hit". Same two tones as the listing badge.

uiElements.label: Leg actual pill
uiElements.description: The number the player actually put up, in its own Actual column directly after the leg. Green beat the line, red did not. One fixed width whatever the number, so the colour blocks stay a column down the page. The column is rendered only when at least one leg that week has been graded.

nodes.label: Explore results
nodes.description: Served at /explore. Every graded shortlisted leg across every week, grouped by a chosen category with an optional one-category filter. Server side is explore_html() in scripts/serve_reports.py, which grades through grade_legs (same rule as the listing tallies and the slate) and embeds the legs as window.__EXPLORE__; the page itself is templates/explore.html. Legs from games not yet final are counted as pending, never shown -- the pending count is season-wide, not scoped to the current Picks/Group by/Only selection.

uiElements.label: Explore container
uiElements.description: Outer 720px column holding the whole explore page.

uiElements.label: Eyebrow
uiElements.description: 'Graded picks' kicker above the title.

uiElements.label: Title
uiElements.description: 'Explore results'.

uiElements.label: Subtitle
uiElements.description: Defines Needed (the hit rate at which $100 on each leg breaks even -- the group's dollar break-even, not the average implied probability of the prices) and $100 each (flat-stake return), and says what All legs vs Shortlist show.

uiElements.label: Back link
uiElements.description: Back to the report listing at /.

uiElements.label: Control row
uiElements.description: Holds the Group by select and the Only filter pair.

uiElements.label: Picks select
uiElements.description: Scopes the whole page: all legs with a book line (default; picked or not, graded by the same rule), the shortlist subset the model actually picked, or anytime-TD picks. TD picks are never pooled with the others - a different model, one per game. Pending counts are per option. Persists in localStorage 'nflprops-explore'.

uiElements.label: Group by select
uiElements.description: Chooses the category the graded legs are cut by: stat, position, depth role, week, kickoff window, price band, model confidence band, model vs book, opponent defense (model-used) (the report's def multiplier: 1.0 = league average for that position; only covers passing yards, completions and rushing yards -- rushing at half weight -- since DEF_WEIGHT is 0 for receiving yards and receptions, and those legs are left out of this grouping), shortlist rank, team, opponent, player. The choice persists in localStorage 'nflprops-explore'.

uiElements.label: Filter category select
uiElements.description: 'Only' - picks a category to filter by, or All legs. Filling it enables the value select.

uiElements.label: Filter value select
uiElements.description: The value of the filter category to keep, with its leg count.

uiElements.label: Summary line
uiElements.description: Hits/graded, hit rate vs needed, and flat $100 return for the current filter; plus how many legs are still waiting on a final score -- that count is season-wide, not scoped to the current Picks/Group by/Only selection. Also counts void legs (game final but the player has no stat line - he didn't play, a book would void it), also season-wide.

uiElements.label: Results container
uiElements.description: Receives the grouped table, rendered by render() in the page script.

uiElements.label: Grouped table
uiElements.description: One row per group: legs, hits, hit rate with a bar (tick = needed), needed, $100 each. Built at runtime. Every header is a sort button (see explore-sort-header) -- 1st click sorts the rows descending by that column's raw number (A-Z for the label column), 2nd click ascending, 3rd click back to the category's own default order; nulls (a group with no priced legs, shown as — for Needed/$100 each) always sort last. Re-sorting collapses any expanded group. The active sort resets when Group by or Picks changes and otherwise persists in localStorage 'nflprops-explore'.

uiElements.label: Column sort button
uiElements.description: One shared id for all six header buttons (group label, Legs, Hits, Hit rate, Needed, $100 each) -- the anchor is the template string that builds all six, not a single element. Keyboard-operable (a real <button>); aria-sort lives on the parent <th>, not the button. Shows a trailing ▼/▲ on the active column only; inactive headers show no arrow. Styled to inherit the th's mono/10px/uppercase look with no browser button chrome.

uiElements.label: Group row
uiElements.description: Click or Enter expands the legs in that group. Greyed (tr.thin) under 10 legs. Row order is the active column sort when one is set (see explore-sort-header), otherwise the category's default: team/opponent/player/depth role by size, the rest natural band order.

uiElements.label: Expanded legs row
uiElements.description: Inserted under a group row by toggle(); lists each leg newest week first.

uiElements.label: Leg row
uiElements.description: Player (links to its report), team role, week and game; the line, price, and the actual number as a HIT/MISS pill.

uiElements.label: Footer
uiElements.description: Grading rule (same as the listing: actual beats the line, final games only), the under-ten caveat, and which stats the opponent-defense grouping covers.
